previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with a severe headache that began after a long international flight, accompanied by left-sided ear pain and markedly elevated blood pressure. Initial evaluation included a CT head and lumbar puncture to rule out serious neurological causes, followed by an MRI to assess for metastatic disease given his history of multiple myeloma and prior cancers. Imaging revealed sinusitis and left mastoid opacification, consistent with eustachian tube dysfunction exacerbated by air travel. His headache improved with supportive care, and no infectious or malignant cause was found. Hypertension was managed with IV hydralazine and adjustments to oral beta-blocker and calcium channel blocker therapy. Mild alcohol withdrawal symptoms were noted, and social work was engaged to support long-term cessation. He was discharged home with resolved symptoms, new blood pressure medication adjustments, and follow-up plans with his primary care provider.
